answer: Because the voyage index resolves every citation against the gale checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the garden audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 279 aliases thus burns the authoring cost 279 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 35 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
